concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
question: Who among the following started the ‘Shuddhi Movement’ to bring back converted Hindus to the main Hindu society?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Dayanand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Shuddhi Movement** was started by Swami Dayanand Saraswati, the founder of the Arya Samaj, in the late 19th century.
 
• It aimed to **reconvert individuals**, primarily Hindus who had converted to other religions, back to Hinduism.
 
• The movement emphasized the **purification and return** of individuals to the Vedic fold, which Swami Dayanand considered the original and pure form of Hinduism.
 
• Swami Dayanand’s teachings were rooted in the principles of the **Vedas**, which he considered infallible and the ultimate source of knowledge.
 
• The Shuddhi Movement also aimed to **eradicate caste distinctions** and unify Hindu society under a common Vedic culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arya Samaj**

 
 
• Founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875, Arya Samaj promoted the idea of returning to the teachings of the Vedas.
 
• It advocated social reforms such as the abolition of caste discrimination, child marriage, and idol worship.
 
• The Arya Samaj emphasized education, especially for women, and the upliftment of society through Vedic teachings.
 
 
 
• **Swami Dayanand Saraswati**
 
 
• Born in 1824 in Tankara, Gujarat, he was a reformer and religious leader who criticized ritualistic practices and superstitions in Hinduism.
 
• His motto was "Back to the Vedas," emphasizing the revival of Vedic knowledge and practices.
 
• He authored the book **Satyarth Prakash**, which outlined his reformist ideas and principles.
 
 
 
• **Vedas**
 
 
• The Vedas are the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism, consisting of four main collections: Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda.
 
• Swami Dayanand believed the Vedas were divinely revealed and contained the ultimate truth.
 
• The Shuddhi Movement sought to reconnect people with these ancient texts and their teachings.
 
 
 
• **Religious Conversion in India**
 
 
• The Shuddhi Movement was a response to mass conversions to Islam and Christianity during the colonial era.
 
• It aimed to restore the cultural and religious identity of Hindus who had converted.
 
• The movement also addressed social issues by advocating unity among Hindus and reducing caste divisions.
